# Eval Log: Method Guide

**Setup:** see `harness.py`. The test has three isolated roles, each a separate `claude -p` session:

| Role | Model | Sees |
|---|---|---|
| Persona | Sonnet | archetype + secret fact sheet |
| Assistant | Sonnet | method guide + earlier confirmed blocks only |
| Judge | Opus | traps + final blocks only |

**Cases:** `cases/`, generated by an independent agent.
- **dev-1:** open language café; anyone can drop in.
- **dev-2:** school cooking programme; 2 focus groups; funder sets mandatory figures.
- **holdout-1:** blind to the developer, who sees only its score.

**Target:** holdout ≥ 80 % traps, with no increase in user burden (persona turns) and no growth in guide size. At most 5 rounds.

**Known limits:**
- Persona, assistant and judge are the same model family.
- Each case runs once per round, so scores are noisy (±10 pp is plausible).
- The harness simulates the app's UI: agreement in the chat counts as "Übernehmen".

## Results

| Round | Guide words | dev-1 | dev-2 | holdout | Consultant score (d1 / d2 / h) | Persona turns (d1 / d2 / h) | Step 4 hit turn limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| r0 | 16,539 | 60 % | 75 % | 75 % | 6 / 6 / 7 | 94 / 100 / 103 | 3 of 3 |
| r1* | 15,311 | **95 %** | – | 75 % | 8 / – / 7 | **48** / – / **52** | 0 of 2 |

\* r1 uses the cheaper defaults (persona Haiku, judge Sonnet, turn cap 15) and the deadline-free traps, so it is only partly comparable with r0.

## r0: baseline (guide v1, unchanged)

**Harness note:** r0 had two interruptions (the Mac went to sleep, then an empty CLI response). Both were resumed from step checkpoints. After r0, the confirm detection was tightened: a step now ends only on a confirm given directly after a full block.

**Systemic weaknesses:**
1. **Step 4 hit the turn limit in every case.** The assistant walks through each activity, link and assumption one by one, so the second focus group never gets done (dev-2 T8 fail).
2. **Open offers aren't modelled.** In dev-1 the target group stayed "all migrants in the district". There was no split between regulars and occasional visitors, and nobody checked what the existing numbers actually count.
3. **The funder's mandatory figures aren't captured as their own category.**
4. **What happens in practice beyond the application isn't asked** (dev-1: help with official letters wasn't listed as an activity).

**Conflict with a PO decision:** dev-1 T2 and dev-2 T1 expected the report deadline in the measurement frame. **The PO decided on 2026-10-10: no deadlines.** Both traps have been adjusted, and the judge prompt now ignores deadline criteria, which also covers the blind holdout. Comparability with r0 is limited as a result.

## r1: changes (guide 16,539 → 15,266 words)

- **Running example removed** (00-shared §10, section 6 in every step, glossary example column). New rule: examples come only from the person's own project.
- **00-shared §4 "Tempo":**
  - whole drafts instead of single items; ask only about the 1–2 most uncertain points; no per-item confirmations;
  - guideline of 8–12 messages per step or focus group;
  - Why drafts go straight into the draft.
- **00-shared §5.6:** check numbers (where a number comes from and what it counts).
- **Step 0:** practice check (how people take part / what happens beyond the application / team), mandatory figures in the measurement frame, what each data source counts.
- **Step 1:** the target group is the people actually reached, not the catchment population. For open offers, regulars and occasional visitors are looked at separately.
- **Step 3:**
  - "who exactly" instead of "the participants";
  - a reality check instead of "machbar?";
  - goals that depend mainly on outside factors don't become project goals;
  - at most 2 goals per level.
- **Step 4:**
  - flow of 4 messages, with a complete chain draft per focus group;
  - the activities list includes what happens in practice;
  - critical = at most 2 per focus group, where the project is most likely to fail.
- **Step 5:**
  - a separate, labelled list "Pflichtangaben (Geldgeberin)", outside the 6 indicators (**PO-approved 2026-10-10**, PRD F5/F8 updated);
  - candidates decided in one proposal;
  - finished indicators instead of options;
  - every focus group gets a learning question.
- **Step 6:** the whole plan as one table; mandatory figures get a plan row.

## r1: aborted (2026-10-10)

Stopped after step 0 because the Claude usage limit was at 99 %. No results. The guide in `method-guide/` is the untested r1 version; the r0 version is in `runs/r0/guide/`.

## Efficiency changes for later rounds

**The quota cost of r0** was about $11 at API prices across three cases. That is usage from the Claude subscription, not money spent.

**New defaults:**
- Persona: Haiku (r0: Sonnet)
- Judge: Sonnet (r0: Opus)
- Assistant: stays on Sonnet, because it is the role being tested
- At most 15 persona turns per step (r0: 25)

These defaults change comparability with r0. **The first new round is the new baseline.**

**`--from-step N --seed-round rX`** reuses the confirmed blocks of steps < N from an earlier round. Only the changed steps run again. This only makes sense when steps < N haven't changed since rX.

**Cheapest sensible next run:**
- `python3 -I eval/harness.py --round r1 --cases holdout-1 dev-1`
- dev-2 only when step 4/5 changes need checking.

## r1 result (2026-10-10)

- **dev-1:** traps 60 % → 95 %, consultant score 6 → 8, persona turns 94 → 48. Step 4 now takes 5 turns instead of 29. All r0 weaknesses in this case are fixed.
- **holdout-1:** traps 75 % → 75 %, consultant score 7, turns 103 → 52. **Target of ≥ 80 % not reached.**
  - Non-passing traps by step (content stays blind): step 1 (fact partial, quality partial) and step 4 (fact partial, quality fail).
- Quota: about $5 at API prices, versus about $11 for r0.

**Assessment:**
- The user burden has halved and dev-1 improved strongly. The holdout case did not move.
- So part of the dev-1 gain may be overfitting to dev-1, or a more lenient judge or more talkative persona after the model switch.
- The remaining weak points sit in steps 1 and 4.

## r2: real case (2026-10-10)

**Case `lukas-1`:**
- Built from Lukas's real application and grant notice, anonymised and git-ignored.
- The facts about the project in practice are invented (status October 2026). Traps were derived from the developer's own document analysis, so some self-grading bias is possible.
- Guide = r1 + target values for mandatory figures.

**Result:** traps 90 %, consultant score 7, persona turns 47, step 4 did not hit the turn limit. **No deadline in any block** (checked with grep).

**What passed:**
- the 8 mandatory figures and the target-vs-actual format;
- the roles of the two partners;
- the focus on regular participants;
- the SFW as focus group 2;
- no crime-prevention goal (violence prevention handled via fair play);
- "regelmäßig" defined;
- mandatory figures kept separate;
- the data hand-over.

**Half met (fixed in the guide without a re-run):**
- Step 0 now separates the current state from what is planned (2 of 3 neighbourhoods were wrongly listed as active).
- Step 5: a mandatory figure gets a proposed target value even when the funder gives none.
